extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and authors preparing documents with AMS-LaTeX (users with some TeX/LaTeX experience)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical instructions and conventions for creating mathematical documents using the AMS-LaTeX collection (amsart/amsproc/amsbook, amsmath, amsrefs, XY-pic, etc.). Includes recommended package use, environments for theorems/proofs/math displays, cross-referencing, bibliographies, and template guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: \documentclass command and choice of AMS classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you type anything that actually appears in the paper, you must include a \documentclass command. AMS-LATEX provides the document classes amsart, amsproc, and amsbook as replacements for the standard LaTeX document classes article, proc, and book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put \documentclass{amsart} (or amsproc, amsbook) at the very beginning of the file. Use optional arguments like [12pt] to change default type size. If you prefer standard classes (article/proc/book) but want AMS features, include \usepackage{amsmath} after \documentclass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loading optional packages (preamble placement and recommended packages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional packages must be loaded after \documentclass and before \begin{document}; examples of important packages are amsrefs (bibliography), amssymb (AMS fonts/symbols), and XY-pic (commutative diagrams).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example recommended preamble: \documentclass{amsart} \usepackage[lite]{amsrefs} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage[all,cmtip]{xy} \let\objectstyle=\displaystyle. Use 'lite' option for amsrefs to avoid conflicts with XY-pic; omit \let\objectstyle=\displaystyle if you prefer \textstyle nodes in XY diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: \begin{document} and \end{document}
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything that is to appear in the document must appear between \begin{document} and \end{document}. Anything after \end{document} is ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macro definitions (\newcommand) and \usepackage commands belong in the preamble (before \begin{document}). There are no optional arguments for \begin{document}/\end{document}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title, author, address, date and \maketitle usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify title, optional running title, authors, addresses, current address, email, acknowledgements, and date using \title, \author, \address, \curraddr, \email, \thanks, and \date, then call \maketitle after these commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \title[Optional running title]{Actual title} with \\ for linebreaks in the title. For multiple authors use separate \author and \address commands for each. amsart places the author's address at the end of the paper. Use \date{...} or \date{\today}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectioning and labels for cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \section, \subsection, \subsubsection, and their *-forms for unnumbered sections. To make cross-references use \label within the smallest enclosing structure and \ref or \eqref to refer to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels take the number of the smallest enclosing structure. Example: \section{Basic \LaTeX{} stuff}\label{sec:basicstuff} so \ref{sec:basicstuff} prints the section number. Use \subsubsection* for unnumbered headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \emph for italics/emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: The LaTeX convention for italics emphasis is to use \emph rather than switching fonts explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \emph{word} — it toggles italics appropriately (switches out of italics if already in italics) and automatically inserts italic correction when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference mechanics and multiple LaTeX runs
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeX writes and reads auxiliary (.aux) and table-of-contents (.toc) files to fill in cross-references; you may need to run LaTeX multiple times for references and TOC to be correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First run creates .aux/.toc; second run fills references; sometimes a third run is needed if the TOC itself changes page layout. LaTeX prints a warning at the end if labels may have changed — run again until no warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling conventions and commands: \ref, \eqref, \pageref, \cite
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \ref for sections/theorems/etc., \eqref for equation numbers (provides parentheses and upright font), \pageref for page numbers, and \cite (or \cites/\citelist when using amsrefs) for bibliography references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \eqref{key} to get (n) with upright font even inside slanted text. When using amsrefs, \cites sorts and compresses numeric labels automatically; \citelist allows annotated cites; use \ycite and \ocite for author-year variants with amsrefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem/proposition/lemma/definition/etc. environments and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Define theorem environments (thm, cor, lem, prop, defn, rem, ex, notation, terminology) via \newtheorem so they share numbering with displayed equations (same sequence) and are numbered within sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \numberwithin{equation}{section} and declare theorem environments with [equation] so everything (theorems, equations) shares the same counter (e.g., 4.1). Provide optional names and \label inside the environment to refer to the theorem number elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof environment usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \begin{proof} ... \end{proof} for proofs; an optional argument to proof (e.g., \begin{proof}[Proof (sufficiency)]) replaces the word 'Proof'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can give a custom heading such as \begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{pythagthm}] to indicate which theorem is being proved. The proof environment prints the 'Proof.' label and the QED marker at the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics in running text: inline math delimiters
rubrics_metrics.description: For inline mathematics use $...$ or \( ... \); \( \) provides a bit more error checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer \( ... \) if you want extra error checking; be aware of spacing conventions (e.g., use \colon or \to for arrows/relations to get correct spacing around punctuation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed mathematics: appropriate environments and avoiding $$
rubrics_metrics.description: Use equation/equation*, displaymath, \[ ... \], or the amsmath environments (gather, align, multline, etc.) depending on numbering and alignment needs. The use of double dollar signs ($$ ... $$) is deprecated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use equation for numbered single-line displays, equation* or \[ ... \] for unnumbered. For multiple lines with/without alignment, choose gather/gathered, align/aligned, multline, flalign, alignat, split as appropriate. Use * variants to omit numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text inside displayed math: use \text rather than \mbox
rubrics_metrics.description: To include text in displayed mathematics use \text{...} (from amsmath) as it scales correctly in subscripts/superscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \[ X_{n} = \coprod_{\text{monomorphisms $[k]\to[n]$}} S_{k} \]. Prefer \text over \mbox because of size and font handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation labeling and references within equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Label an equation with \label inside the equation environment to refer to it later; use \eqref for references with parentheses in upright font.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \begin{equation}\label{pi1eqn} ... \end{equation} then 'see formula~\eqref{pi1eqn}' yields 'see formula (7.1)'. Labeling each line in multi-line displays is supported (gather/align with \label per line).

rubrics_metrics.name: Displays with alignment: use ampersand & to set alignment points
rubrics_metrics.description: In align/align* and similar environments, use & immediately before the symbol to be aligned across lines; separate lines with \\.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiple columns/alignment points see sections on align, alignat, flalign. Use aligned/alignedat/gathered when embedding aligned blocks inside a larger display. Optional [t] or [b] arguments control vertical alignment of embedded aligned/gathered blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of amsrefs for bibliographies (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the amsrefs package to create bibliographies; it provides \bib{key}{TypeOfItem}{...} entries and integrates with \cite commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Load with \usepackage[lite]{amsrefs}. Create items with \bib{HA}{book}{author={...}, title={...}, ...}. Use \cites to sort/compress multiple numeric citations; use author-year option and \ycite/\ocite when appropriate. 'lite' avoids automatic loading of mathscinet/txtcmds to prevent conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using an external reference database with amsrefs: .ltb and \bibselect
rubrics_metrics.description: Put many \bib commands into a .ltb file (each \bib begins on a new line with its first two arguments) and use \bibselect{myrefs} to extract only those cited in the current paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create myrefs.ltb containing many \bib entries; in your paper use \begin{bibdiv}\begin{biblist}\bibselect{myrefs}\end{biblist}\end{bibdiv}. Use \bibselect*{myrefs} to list all items whether cited or not. Multiple .ltb files can be comma-separated in \bibselect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using amsrefs with BibTeX
rubrics_metrics.description: You can combine BibTeX with amsrefs: load amsrefs (with lite) in the preamble and use \bibliography{myrefs} where you want the bibliography to appear. BibTeX will create a .bbl containing bibdiv/biblist for LaTeX to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run BibTeX as usual; do not use \bibliographystyle (it will be ignored). The .bbl produced will include bibdiv and biblist environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding both amsrefs and BibTeX: thebibliography and \bibitem
rubrics_metrics.description: If you don't want to use amsrefs or BibTeX, create bibliography items manually using the thebibliography environment and \bibitem{key}Item entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with \begin{thebibliography}{number} where 'number' is as wide as the widest label (e.g., '99' if between 10 and 99 items). Each item: \bibitem{yellowmonster} A. K. Bousfield... . Use \cite{yellowmonster} to reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options and conflicts for the amsrefs package
rubrics_metrics.description: amsrefs has options (lite, initials, alphabetic, shortalphabetic, y2k, author-year) that control formatting; the 'lite' option avoids loading mathscinet/txtcmds to prevent conflicts with XY-pic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'lite' is recommended to avoid a \cir conflict between txtcmds and XY-pic. If you need mathscinet/txtcmds plus XY-pic, load amsrefs before XY-pic (\usepackage{amsrefs} then \usepackage[all,cmtip]{xy}). Use alphabetic/shortalphabetic to get alpha-style labels; use author-year to suppress labels and get author-year citations (then use \ycite/\ocite).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutative diagrams with XY-pic
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the XY-pic package to draw commutative diagrams in LaTeX directly; load with \usepackage[all,cmtip]{xy} and set node style with \let\objectstyle=\displaystyle or omit to use \textstyle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections provide many diagram techniques: basic diagrams, spacing, shifting nodes, arrow styles, curved arrows, nodes off the grid, text objects, annotations, etc. Load XY-pic in the preamble; remember amsrefs 'lite' avoids conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including graphics and figure environment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To import graphics use the graphicx package (\usepackage{graphicx}) and put images inside a figure environment to allow floating; place \label after \caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \begin{figure}[h] ... \includegraphics{filename} \caption{Some caption} \label{somelabel} \end{figure}. Ensure graphicx is loaded in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro definitions: place \newcommand in the preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Define macros (\newcommand, \DeclareMathOperator, etc.) in the preamble (after \documentclass and before \begin{document}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template includes many example commands such as \newcommand{\R}{\mathbb{R}} and \DeclareMathOperator*{\colim}{colim}. Keep macro definitions in the preamble to affect the whole document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the provided template file as a starting point
rubrics_metrics.description: A template (template.tex) is provided and reproduced in the notes; it contains common package loading, theorem environment declarations, macros, bibliography scaffolding, and examples of usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the template to 'fake your way through an AMS-LATEX file' and refer to the table of contents of these instructions for further details. The template demonstrates numbering, theorem styles, and the structure for bibdiv/biblist or thebibliography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering strategy: numberwithin and sharing counters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \numberwithin{equation}{section} so equations are numbered within sections and share the equation counter with theorem environments by defining theorems with [equation].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This causes Theorems, Propositions, Lemmas, Definitions, Remarks, Examples, Notations, Terminologies, and displayed equations to be numbered in the same sequence (SectionNumber.Number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for multiple-author running heads and names
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple authors make the running head too long, supply an optional short form to each \author command for running heads; convention often uses initials for first/middle names in running heads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \author[P.S. Hirschhorn]{Philip S. Hirschhorn}. Supply separate \author and \address blocks per author; include \thanks, \email, \curraddr as needed.
